name: rsa_animate
drawing_speed_note: Centre-line ink length in 4K scene pixels per second. Starting value from 2026-09-27 calibration: the four approved Chapter 2 scenes held 74k-96k px of centre-line ink for about 16-18 s of narration. Tuned by hand when needed (no gate asks about it since D79; it also sets the scene budgets, so a change means render_scenes.py sync, then the video is rebuilt).
fill_width_note: Ink wider than this (4K px) is a fill and is wiped. Measured 2026-09-27 on a 4K scene: lines 12-18 px, lettering 25-40 px, speed lines 44-50 px, solid areas 75-220 px.
schedule_note: stitch.py global pen (D59, D82): the title draws first in exactly title_draw_s (its own stroke/fill times scaled to fit) in a silent lead-in of title_draw_s + title_gap_s, then every segment in story order starts at max(its speech start, previous draw end + a gap), + lead_in_s for the first story segment. The gap is camera.dwell_s (+ the glide lead when a flow arrow leads in) before the first segment of a camera shot, and 0 (+ camera.arrow_draw_s for a flow arrow drawn in the held frame) between segments of one shot. A segment that would end later than the next sentence's start - the next gap draws faster, just enough, at most camera.max_speedup x drawing_speed_px_s; otherwise segments keep drawing_speed_px_s. A narration pause is inserted only when a segment would start more than segment_overlap_s after its sentence.
density_band_note: Each segment's drawing time (reveal.py analysis at drawing_speed_px_s) is compared with 75-125% of its sentence's available time (user, 2026-09-27). density_mode 'warn' (D77, user, 2026-09-30): a miss is recorded as density_warnings on the verdict and never fails an attempt; the board video absorbs it with max_speedup and short pauses. 'fail' restores the old rule (a miss fails the attempt and adds a generated fix).
layout_note: stitch.py board step (`stitch.py board`, D58/D78/D79; source 4K px = board px at scale 1): every segment (connector arrows removed, D60) and the title are pieces trimmed to their ink, with seeded scale and tilt (the title keeps scale 1). Segments of one scene drawn on or inside each other in the scene image are glued into one rigid compound (D83, user 2026-10-01: the CAST lines left their clipboard, the three steps left their staircase): two segments glue when one's mask ink dilated by glue.touch_px covers at least glue.min_contact_px of the other's, or when at least glue.inside_share of the smaller ink bbox lies inside the other's (chains glue too). A compound shares its first member's scale and tilt, keeps every member where the scene image has it and is packed as one unit at its first member's place in story order; its members are still drawn one by one with their own masks, reveal order, shots and camera, and no flow arrow joins two members. Measured on a test run (4K px, touch 8): touching segments 663-20773 px of contact against 47 px for a corner graze; contained ones 0.99-1.0 inside against 0.54 at most for neighbours. The pieces (compounds as one) are split into 2-5 rows balanced by area and packed in story order along a serpentine (title top-left) inside a 16:9 frame, each piece touching its predecessor with its ink dilated by gap_px/2; a gravity pass then pulls every piece toward the middle. The smallest 16:9 board over frame widths x row counts wins (board = all ink + margin_px, widened to 16:9). Then board-level flow arrows (user 2026-10-01) fill the blank spots: only in a gap of at least arrows.min_gap_px between two pieces consecutive in story order (piece i -> i+1, or the last of scene n -> the first of n+1), pointing from the earlier to the later one through the gap's widest point, widest gaps first, at most arrows.max; each is a seeded hand-drawn marker arrow (width_px, colour seeded from palette.json arrows, slight wobble, open or filled head), min_len_px..max_len_px long, keeping clearance_px from the dilated ink, the board edge and the other arrows (arrows.seed picks the style). The board (videos/board.png + videos/board_layout.json) is approved at Gate 2 before any video frame is rendered; edits there change these values (seed, gap_px, margin_px, scale, tilt_deg, arrows.*, glue.*) and the board is rebuilt.
camera_note: stitch.py camera (D61, shots D82; seconds; hold_pad = share of the framed size added on each side): the window is never narrower than 1920 x the largest piece scale (board px). Shots (D82, user Gate 3 r1 2026-10-01: the constant pan and zoom on every segment was tiring): the title is a shot of its own, then each scene's segments are split into shots of shot_size consecutive segments (2 or 3; 4 -> 2+2, 5 -> 3+2 or 2+3, 3 -> 3, 2 -> 2, a one-segment scene alone); a shot never spans a scene change, so every scene change is still a glide. A shot's window frames all of its pieces and the flow arrows between them (union + hold_pad) and may be at most max_shot_window_frac x the board width; among the valid splits of a scene the tightest framings win, and a scene with no valid split falls back to single-segment shots where needed. The window holds still on the shot while its 2-3 segments draw in turn (an arrow between two of them is drawn by the pen right before the later one, in the held frame), rests dwell_s after the shot's last segment (the pen waits the same; max_speedup lets a late segment draw faster so the rest costs no narration time), then makes ONE glide to the next shot: it starts at max(draw end + dwell_s, next draw start - move_s/2) and lasts move_s, passing through a window centred on the two pieces either side of the cut that is at least the geometric mean of the two shot widths (a gentle push-in or pull-out, eased in log width), and always holds every stroke of the new shot drawn so far. A flow arrow between two shots is drawn by the pen in arrow_draw_s (<= move_s), shaft then head, centred on the middle of that glide; that glide starts arrow_draw_s/2 earlier, the piece starts no earlier than the previous draw end + dwell_s + (move_s + arrow_draw_s)/2, and the window widens where needed to hold the whole arrow (+ hold_pad x the minimum window), eased in from the glide's start and out by its end. The zoom-out to the whole board starts at max(last draw end, last speech end) + max(end_hold_s, dwell_s), lasts end_zoom_s, then holds end_final_hold_s.
detail_tiers_note: Bands set 2026-09-27 so the typical 12-22 s scene range spreads across all three tiers (sparse <= ~14 s of drawing, dense > ~18 s).

detail_tiers.name: sparse
detail_tiers.prompt: Keep the drawing sparse: simple outline-level figures and objects, very little interior detail, no hatching, lots of open white space.

detail_tiers.name: medium
detail_tiers.prompt: Use moderate detail: clear figures and objects with some interior detail and a little hatching on the main figure only.

detail_tiers.name: dense
detail_tiers.prompt: Use rich detail: fuller figures, interior detail, light hatching and small supporting marks, while keeping every element separated by white space.
